business_problem: Factory needed secure observability and a faster feedback loop for autonomous SDLC agents running inside enterprise environments with strict privacy controls, custom LLM tooling, and limited tolerance for opaque debugging workflows.
solution_summary: Factory runs AI Droids that automate stages of the software development lifecycle and uses self-hosted LangSmith as the observability backbone inside tightly controlled customer environments. LangSmith traces are exported into AWS CloudWatch so engineers can correlate agent events with infrastructure logs and follow data through each step of a multi-stage LLM pipeline without building a proprietary logging stack. Feedback is attached directly to individual LLM calls through the Feedback API, then exported into datasets for analysis. Factory’s engineers use custom LangChain tooling to compare good and bad code-review comments, hypothesize why prompts failed, re-prompt the model, and improve accuracy. This closed-loop design lets the team keep enterprise data private while continuously tuning Code Droid and related Droids from production evidence rather than ad hoc manual review.

data_flow: Droids execute SDLC tasks, Self-hosted LangSmith records each LLM step and exports traces to AWS CloudWatch, engineers attach workflow feedback through the Feedback API, and custom LangChain tooling turns those labeled examples into prompt updates and new runs that can be evaluated again.
business_outcome: Factory doubled iteration speed for prompt and agent improvement, reduced open-to-merge time and code churn for customers, and established a secure, enterprise-friendly observability stack for autonomous engineering workflows.
